propositions: ADR corpus contains 91 files with only 69 distinct numbers; 17 numbers are duplicated across 22 files, causing ambiguity in references and preventing collision detection.
Current numbering scheme has no mechanism to prevent or detect same-number additions; pre-merge CI checks are racy against server-side rebases, making marker files the only race-free solution.
Cross-references to ADRs by bare number (e.g. 'ADR 0037') or slug-bearing links ('adr/NNNN-slug') can become stale or ambiguous when numbers are reused, requiring systematic sweep and resolution.
Renumbering moves 22 duplicate-numbered ADRs to range 0070-0091 (ascending landing-date order), while earliest-landed ADR in each collision group retains its original number.

Per-number marker files and generated index restore bijection between ADRs and numbers; CI gate asserts unique numbers, marker-content uniqueness, and referential integrity of all adr/NNNN-slug links in docs/
